scope: Adjacent demand and inference-cost observations, not a standalone structured-decision-model market-size estimate or proof of net deployment gains.

56.title: AI Index Report 2025
56.evidence_type: Report synthesis of surveys and cost research, not this project's survey

57.title: Anthropic Economic Index: September 2025 report
57.evidence_type: Vendor analysis of its own sampled first-party API records

observations.denominator: Organizations in the underlying survey summarized by the report
observations.supports: AI is entering business workflows, creating potential demand for software-consumable judgments.
observations.does_not_establish: All-firm population penetration, structured-decision-model adoption, revenue, or ROI.

observations.unit: Sampled first-party API prompt-response pair, possibly mid-session; not a firm or unique user
observations.sampling_frame: A customer pool accounting for roughly half of Anthropic's first-party API usage
observations.measure: Privacy-preserving classification of automation interaction patterns
observations.supports: Programmatic task delegation is an observed usage pattern among this vendor's sampled customers.
observations.does_not_establish: 77% of enterprises adopting automation, 77% successful task completion, industry-wide penetration, or this category's share.

observations.measure: Inference cost for a system performing at GPT-3.5 level
observations.supports: Lower deployment barriers, while competing generative-model baselines also become cheaper.
observations.does_not_establish: Jev/NanoJev/Laya speedup, their current prices, or a guaranteed hybrid cost advantage.

interpretation: Community releases indicate developer interest and multiple implementation paths; release timing is not development duration or customer adoption.
The reviewed sources do not provide a consistently defined independent TAM for structured decision models.
Adoption requires avoided work to exceed added judgment, operations and error-recovery costs at the same quality target and accounting scope.
Anthropic's report also highlights capability fit, contextual information and economic task value; low model price alone is not evidence of demand or ROI.
